problem: The figure shows a UV detector at 280 nm in a generic chromatography diagram. GC uses a flame ionisation detector, and UV detection is specific to HPLC/protein work, so a student may think every chromatograph uses a UV detector.
fix: Label the figure as an HPLC example, or write 'detector' generically and note that GC uses a flame ionisation detector.

problem: Retention time is defined as the time from injection to the peak maximum. Injection applies to column methods (GC and HPLC). TLC and paper chromatography use Rf values, so the definition can mislead a student applying it to a plate or sheet.
fix: State that tR applies to column chromatography; for TLC and paper chromatography, use the Rf value (distance moved by solute divided by distance moved by solvent front).

problem: 'SDS-PAGE binds SDS' is awkward and technically imprecise: SDS-PAGE is the technique, and SDS is the detergent that binds to proteins.
fix: In SDS-PAGE, SDS binds to proteins, masks their intrinsic charge and gives them a similar negative charge per unit mass.

problem: The friction factor is written as 'N per m/s'. A student may read this as (N/m)/s rather than N·s/m.
fix: Write f as the friction factor in N·s/m (equivalently kg/s).
